title: BLOATMAXX: the Kyriakos Grizzly example, mogging general & potential downsides
summary: Using the 4chan bloatmaxxing meme and Kyriakos Grizzly, NH examines the age-old practice of piling on mass. He grants that bloat increases strength and leverage, then lists the downsides for naturals: mostly visceral fat, inflated strength masking real progress, poorer conditioning, shifting technique, lower testosterone and worse health. He endorses slow bulks of 1-2 lb a month.
claims: Bloatmaxxing started as a 4chan meme but reflects an age-old practice of packing on mass, mostly fat and water
Mass moves mass: gaining 100 lb at 200 lb raises all your lifts
Novice programs that push rapid weight gain produce strength carried by bloat, not just muscle
Strongmen and super-heavyweight powerlifters bloatmax for strength; they're massive but not jacked
Bloat has a limit: taller, bigger-framed people can carry more, but eventually extra mass prevents lifting
He was once 240 lb at six feet with a narrow frame, and his body already suffered at that weight
Even sumo wrestlers must watch weight, or they become slow and unstable
Bloatmaxxing is the logical extreme of bear mode; he fell into it and came back down after realizing his mistake
No one bulks 100 lb and gets 90% muscle; getting fat is easy, getting muscular takes effort
Excessive fat becomes visceral (waist, lower back, love handles), which isn't aesthetic
Pros can bloat in the offseason and keep muscle when cutting because of drugs; naturals can't
After big natural bulks you think you have 20 lb of fat to lose but it's really 40
The theory that all big naturals got very fat is wrong; they slow-bulked for years and the fat phase came at the end when things went wrong
Slow bulking is the best way for naturals to get big
Aggressive bulks create artificial strength progress, breaking strength as a proxy for muscle growth
Bulk and cut slowly, about 1-2 lb a month; recomping may be the answer for many
Fat improves pressing leverage by shortening range of motion; he benched 315 at about 220 lb and doubts he could at 190
Super heavyweights' squat and bench benefit from the belly, while the gut makes the deadlift harder and often weaker than their squat
Fat adds weight without vascularity, hurting cardiovascular endurance; muscle brings veins and oxygen delivery
People at 350 lb aren't healthy even at 6% body fat; health and longevity are everything
Weight changes alter your squat, deadlift and bench technique, so aggressive bulk/cut cycles force constant relearning
Poor conditioning leads to fewer reps, sets and supersets, skewing training toward low-rep intensity and lowering tonnage
Many strength athletes now recomp to lower weight classes, prioritizing quality mass over quantity
Bodybuilding is form over function and powerlifting function over form, but both grow the same tissue
Getting obese as a natural lowers testosterone production; you might even lose muscle on an extreme bulk
Bloatmaxxers eat junk food for calories, which ruins health
Endless bulk/cut cycling isn't the way to get big; extremes are bad in any direction
NoFap and semen retention started as 4chan jokes that some took seriously
Naturals naturally gain some intramuscular fat as they build muscle; no need to focus on getting fat
